etymologies.etymologyHTML: From spice +‎ -y, attested since the 16th century.

definitions.definition: Of, pertaining to, or containing spice.
(informal, of flavors) Provoking a burning sensation due to the presence of capsaicin.
(of foods, flavors, or odors) Tangy, zesty, or pungent.

quote.citation: 1769, Firishta, translated by Alexander Dow, Tales translated from the Persian of Inatulla of Delhi, volume I, Dublin: P. and W. Wilson et al., page iv:
quote.text: The breath of the mountain heifer was fragrant as the gales of Sirendiep, by feeding on ſpicy herbs.

definitions.definition: (of expression or behavior) Vigorous; colorful; stimulating.

quote.citation: 1847 January – 1848 July, William Makepeace Thackeray, Vanity Fair […], London: Bradbury and Evans […], published 1848, →OCLC:
quote.text: When one side or the other had written any particularly spicy dispatch, news of it was sure to slip out.

definitions.definition: (Internet slang) Risky; mildly aggressive or dangerous.
(Internet slang) Risqué, sexy, racy; mildly pornographic.
